corrections.post: someone who might want to keep their pilates routine consistent and on the go
corrections.reason: Subsumption holds: keeping a pilates routine is a specific way of being into health. PRE is substantive but the POST is a concrete behavioral subset of the health-interest category, not a sibling domain. Narrowed is defensible; pass 1 is correct.

Subsumption test fails: 'someone who travels frequently is a specific way of being an active person' is not literally true. Frequent travel is not a subset of activeness — many active people never travel, and many travelers are sedentary. Both occupy activity/lifestyle territory but with different organizing frames: PRE frames around general physical/active engagement, POST frames around mobility/travel behavior. Sibling concepts, not subsumption. Reframed is correct; original conflation with the pilates-travel context should not bleed into this pairing.
